title: Partition, format and mount a new disk

DISK.means: the new, empty disk, e.g. sdb

PART.means: the partition created on it, e.g. sdb1

MOUNT.means: the folder to mount it on, e.g. /data

steps.say: Find the new disk: TYPE disk, no partitions, no FSTYPE, no mount point.
One GPT partition filling the disk. This erases the disk.
steps.cmd: sudo parted -s /dev/<DISK> mklabel gpt mkpart primary ext4 0% 100%
steps.rollback: No undo: the old partition table is gone.

steps.say: Create an ext4 filesystem on the new partition.
steps.rollback: No undo: whatever was on the partition is gone.

steps.say: Add this line at the end of /etc/fstab. nofail lets the server boot even if the disk is missing.
Check /etc/fstab for mistakes. Fix any error before going on.
Tell systemd about the changed fstab.
Mount everything in fstab: the same as a reboot would.

pitfalls: A wrong fstab line can stop the next boot. Never skip findmnt --verify and mount -a.
